skill.name: writing-lib-functions
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants to write small, modular library functions for a Next.js app under `srs/lib`.
skill.summary: Write modular Next.js library functions with concise file organization rules.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around a directory path. No executable code, shell invocation, network access, environment access, or prompt injection was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: description: Use this skill when you need to write lib functions in `srs/lib` for the Next.js app
- Follow the rules below to write lib functions in `srs/lib` for the Next.js app:

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 3 uses backticks as Markdown inline code around the `srs/lib` path. There is no executable Ruby or shell context.
Line 8 uses backticks as Markdown inline code around the `srs/lib` path. It is prose guidance, not command execution.

content.value_statement: Next.js utility code can become large and hard to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create modular lib functions.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of library functions for a Next.js app.
Directs work toward the `srs/lib` directory named in the skill.
Encourages modular functions instead of large combined files.
Sets a maximum file size guideline of 50 lines.
Suggests splitting library functions across multiple files when useful.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts, templates, or generated source files.
Does not validate imports, tests, framework version, or project structure.
References `srs/lib`, so users should confirm the intended project path.
Provides broad style rules, not detailed architecture guidance.

use_cases.title: Add a Utility Function
use_cases.description: Create a focused helper for a Next.js feature while keeping the file small and reusable.

use_cases.title: Organize Shared Logic
use_cases.description: Split repeated business logic into separate library files with clear responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Review AI Generated Helpers
use_cases.description: Ask an AI assistant to reshape utility code so each file stays concise and modular.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Helper
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single library function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-lib-functions skill to create one small Next.js helper for this task: [describe task]. Keep it modular and suitable for `srs/lib`.

prompt_templates.title: Split Shared Logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to organize repeated logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-lib-functions skill to move this repeated logic into modular library functions under `srs/lib`: [paste description]. Keep each file concise.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing Utilities
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve existing utility structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-lib-functions skill to review these existing helpers and propose a modular file split. Keep every suggested file under 50 lines.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Lib Function Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple related helpers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-lib-functions skill to design a small set of related Next.js lib functions for [feature]. Separate responsibilities across files when useful.

output_examples.input: Create a helper for formatting display dates in a Next.js app.
output: A focused date utility is placed under the requested lib area.
The helper has one clear responsibility and a small file footprint.
Related formatting concerns are kept separate when they grow.

output_examples.input: Refactor several repeated string helpers into shared library functions.
output: Repeated string logic is grouped into reusable utility files.
Each file stays concise and avoids mixing unrelated helpers.
The assistant explains where each helper belongs.

best_practices: Confirm the actual lib directory before applying the skill.
Keep each helper focused on one responsibility.
Ask for tests or usage examples when the project requires them.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated helpers into one large utility file.
Do not exceed the 50 line file guideline without a clear reason.
Do not treat the skill as a replacement for project-specific architecture rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides AI assistants to write small, modular library functions for a Next.js app.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains only Markdown instructions and no scripts.

faq.question: Does it enforce the 50 line rule automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the assistant to follow the rule, but it does not run validation.

faq.question: Can it create multiple files?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions recommend separating lib functions into multiple files when possible.

faq.question: Should users verify the `srs/lib` path?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill references `srs/lib`, so users should confirm that this path matches their project.
